claim: pyGigEVision is MIT-licensed, requires Python >=3.10, and depends only on numpy>=1.20 and psutil>=5.9
Pure-Python GVCP/GVSP implementation over stdlib sockets; no vendor SDK, GenTL/Harvesters or Aravis dependency

Maintenance: created 2026-05-11, last commit 2026-07-08 (v0.2.2); PyPI releases 0.0.1 (2026-05-12), 0.2.1 (2026-06-11), 0.2.2 (2026-07-08); 6 stars; ~67/69 commits by one author; 2 open PRs from 2026-10-20 (pixel cap, macOS firewall)
how_verified: other: git log on clone, PyPI JSON API, gh api repos/ladisk/pyGigEVision

claim: No GenICam XML parsing or feature-by-name access; XML is downloaded only and parsing is left to vendor drivers
No PTP (IEEE 1588), no action commands, no WRITEMEM method, no event channel, no multicast support
how_verified: read-code + grep -rniE 'ptp|1588|action|multicast|writemem' over the whole repo (only constant CMD_WRITEMEM defined, never used)

claim: Only unpacked Mono8/10/12/14/16 pixel formats are supported; unknown formats default to 2 bytes/pixel uint16, so BayerRG8 and RGB8 frames come back mis-sized (614400 bytes vs expected 307200/921600) and never complete
how_verified: ran-test: docker run pygev-test (python:3.12-bookworm + aravis-tools 0.8.26) arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8 -i eth0; python -I /scripts/t3_grab.py --fmt BayerRG8|RGB8

claim: Frames larger than 2048*2048 pixels are silently dropped (2448x2048 and 2592x1944 not delivered)
how_verified: ran-test: python -I /scripts/t9_max_pixels.py in Docker (synthetic GVSP sender)

claim: parse_first_url treats digit-only bare-hex addresses as decimal (and a unit test enshrines this), so bootstrap() against Aravis's fake camera (URL 'Local:arv-fake-camera.xml;10000;3e67') reads address 10000 decimal and returns 15975 zero bytes instead of the XML; Aravis parses these fields base-16
how_verified: ran-test: t1_discover_xml.py and t2_xml_workaround.py against arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8 in Docker

claim: GVSPReceiver requests a 16 MB SO_RCVBUF but silently ignores the cap; on Linux default it is 425,984 bytes, yielding 1/43 (Mono8) and 0/49 (Mono16) complete 640x480@30 frames from the fake camera, while Aravis got 91/91 and 82/82; with SO_RCVBUFFORCE 32 MB pyGigEVision got 83/83 and 88/88
how_verified: ran-test: t3_grab.py with and without --force-rcvbuf 16777216 (--cap-add NET_ADMIN); t4_aravis_baseline.py via /usr/bin/python3 + gir1.2-aravis-0.8

claim: With a large buffer, a single pyGigEVision receiver sustained ~197 MB/s (1080p100, 1500B packets, ~49% of one core) and ~248 MB/s (2048x2048@60, 9000B packets, ~21%) from the loopback fake camera with 100% complete frames; with default Linux buffers it delivered 0% complete frames at these rates while Aravis's UDP-socket path delivered 94%/90% at 1500B packets using 8-14% CPU
how_verified: ran-test: t3_grab.py --fmt Mono8 --w/--h/--fps/--pkt matrix, and t5_aravis_rate.py with --cap-drop NET_RAW, in Docker

claim: Two GVSPReceivers in one Python process scale poorly (1080p100/1500B: ~20 fps each, 115% CPU) consistent with GIL contention; two separate processes each reach ~100% complete at ~200 MB/s
how_verified: ran-test: t6_multicam.py (one process) and two concurrent t3_grab.py --ip processes, two arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8 instances on eth0 + dummy0

claim: Gap detection marks every not-yet-received packet as missing once a frame is >5 ms old, so a lossless sender paced at 110 MB/s triggered resend requests for 82.6% of all packets (and reports them as 'recovered'); Aravis only considers packets below the highest received packet id
how_verified: ran-test: t7_paced_resend.py 110e6/280e6/1000e6 in Docker (listener on 127.0.0.1:3956 counting PACKETRESEND)

claim: With GEV 2.x extended IDs, a gap in any block with block_id > 65535 raises an uncaught struct.error in _send_resend_direct, killing the receiver thread silently (get_frame returns None thereafter)
how_verified: ran-test: t8_extended_id.py in Docker; traceback 'struct.error: 'H' format requires 0 <= number <= 65535', receiver_thread_alive=False

claim: Frame timestamps are exposed only as the raw 64-bit leader tick count; tick frequency (bootstrap 0x093C/0x0940) is not read by the library (fake camera reports 1 GHz when read manually; leader deltas 33,333,000 ticks at 30 fps)
Tests are 85 mock-based unit tests with no hardware/emulator integration; CI runs ubuntu-latest and windows-latest on Python 3.10-3.13, no macOS
how_verified: ran-test: python -m pytest -q in Docker -> 85 passed in 0.39s; read-code

claim: Aravis fake GV camera implements only DISCOVERY/READMEM/WRITEMEM/READREG/WRITEREG (no PACKETRESEND, no PTP, no action commands), so resend recovery, PTP and actions cannot be tested with it
